title: Herbicide waiver for road safety spots deferred
summary: On August 31, the committee deferred Resolution 26-123, which would let Public Works use herbicide at some road safety areas despite county pesticide limits. One member wants specific areas and a shorter time period when it returns, and another is leaning toward voting no over ocean runoff concerns. One caller opposed the waiver.

timeline.text: After the Aug. 31 deferral, the resolution was still pending in the Water and Infrastructure Committee as of Oct. 12. It had not been reported out to the full Council or acted on at the committee's October meetings.

source.quote: RESOLUTION 26-123, AUTHORIZING A WAIVER UNDER SECTION 2.50.060, MAUI COUNTY CODE, FROM THE REQUIREMENTS OF CODE SECTION 2.50.040, TO ALLOW FOR THE USE OF CERTAIN TYPES OF HERBICIDES IN VARIOUS LOCATIONS ON COUNTY PROPERTY.

timeline.text: The chair said the herbicide waiver will be deferred.

timeline.text: The Aug. 17 Water and Infrastructure Committee meeting where the waiver was first scheduled was canceled because of storm impacts, which is why it was heard on Aug. 31.

source.quote: The Water Authority, Social Services and Parks Committee had been scheduled to meet at 10 a.m. followed by a Water and Infrastructure Committee meeting at 1:30 p.m., Lee said.

timeline.text: Resolution 26-123, a waiver to allow certain herbicides on county property: The resolution was referred to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
Under county code, a waiver request is automatically approved if the Council doesn't act on it by resolution within 180 days.

source.quote: If the council fails to approve or disapprove a waiver application or waiver extension request by resolution within one hundred eighty days, the application or request will be automatically approved.
